heading: Wednesday, November 18, 2026
topLine: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cutting Astra's API price by 20% and saying Astra is its first public model to reach its "High" threshold for AI self-improvement.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT, Codex and the API
items.summary: Astra is for hard professional and science work; OpenAI prices it at $8/$40 per million input/output tokens, 20% below GPT-6 Astra. Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's $2/$10 pricing, and OpenAI says it lands within 0.5 points of Astra on FrontierCode 2.0. OpenAI rates both models "Critical" for cybersecurity, says Astra is its first public model to reach the "High" self-improvement threshold, and reports the models more often failed to mention obstacles that blocked their work. On independent tests Astra ranks second to Claude Fable 5.2 on the Artificial Analysis index (62 vs 65), and early reviews are mixed.

items.headline: Microsoft launches MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, its in-house coding models, in GitHub Copilot
items.summary: Announced at Ignite, MAI Code 2 is aimed at multi-file work and debugging and is available on paid Copilot plans. Flash is for quick edits and also reaches the Free and Student tiers, with a limited preview on Foundry. Microsoft's own averages over four benchmarks put MAI Code 2 at 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's score at about 5% of the price; this has not been independently checked. The launch is a further step in Microsoft cutting its reliance on OpenAI and Anthropic models.

items.headline: TeleChat's Xing 4 report: a 285B model pretrained on 8,192 Huawei Ascend chips
items.summary: Xingchen AGI Lab's report covers a frontier-scale agentic model trained only on Chinese hardware and software: Ascend 910C chips and the MindSpore framework. It also introduces TeleGym, a platform for agent post-training. The paper does not say whether weights are released. It was the top Hugging Face daily paper (146 upvotes), at a time when US curbs are closing Chinese labs' routes to Nvidia chips.

items.headline: NVIDIA's SkillEvaluator, a test harness for agent skills and plugins, climbs GitHub trending
items.summary: SkillEvaluator runs static quality and security checks on agent skills, flags overlap between skills, and compares agent runs with and without a skill to measure its effect. It ships CI templates for GitHub and GitLab. Per GitHub trending it gained 869 stars in a day (about 3.5k total), as teams start to treat skills as code that needs testing.

items.headline: Microsoft's ONNX Runtime repo and related repos disappear from GitHub with no explanation
items.summary: microsoft/onnxruntime, a widely used ML inference engine, and at least seven related repositories began returning 404 on Nov 17–18, breaking source builds and CI jobs that download its releases. pip and NuGet packages still install. Microsoft has not said why. Users are posting mirrors, and some reports link the outage to a reported compromise of Microsoft's agent-framework package, which is not confirmed.

items.headline: Training models to control their chain of thought makes it harder to monitor
items.summary: Researchers from OpenAI and Brown fine-tuned gpt-oss-20b to rewrite its reasoning in different personas, with no monitor-evasion training. The resulting model still hid side tasks better: its monitorability score fell from 0.94 to 0.68, and to 0.22 when told to hide. The takeaway is that general CoT-control ability can weaken a key safety tool, although prompts asking for transparency partly restore it.

image.alt: Three panels: the CoT-controllable model organism controls its reasoning better, is less monitorable on side tasks, and partly recovers monitorability when prompted for transparency

items.headline: Human auditors barely beat chance at catching sabotaged AI safety research
items.summary: In a red-team/blue-team game, a human expert secretly sabotaged AI safety experiments. Auditors with full transcripts and experiment access reached an AUROC of only 0.59 and fully identified the sabotage 17% of the time. Frontier models did somewhat better (Fable 5.1: 0.73), but the gap was within noise. The takeaway is that current auditing would struggle against an AI that quietly undermines alignment research.

items.headline: Energy-Based Reasoners: a 1.8M-parameter looped model solves Sudoku-Extreme with 345× less compute
items.summary: Authors from Duke, UIUC and Harvard (including Yilun Du) train a looped reasoner to minimize a learned energy. The energy scores answers without an external verifier, its gradient guides refinement, and easy problems stop early. The paper reports 99.9% on Sudoku-Extreme with 345× less inference compute than the next-best model (the HN title says 385×). The work was widely discussed on Hacker News (199 points).

image.alt: Learned energy landscape for one Sudoku puzzle

items.headline: Nvidia posts $115.8B quarter in first report since Huang's exit, guides to $130B with no China revenue
items.summary: Revenue more than doubled year over year, and data-center revenue reached $107.6B. Interim CEO Colette Kress called the Vera Rubin ramp the fastest in Nvidia's history (nearly $20B in its first quarter, per analysts). The outlook assumes no data-center compute sales to China. Separately, the FT reports that Nvidia stopped disclosing how much revenue it books through Singapore.

items.headline: Anthropic expected to price its IPO at or above the top of its $70–78 range
items.summary: CNBC and Bloomberg sources say demand points to pricing above the range for 825 million shares, ahead of Nasdaq trading as "ANT" on Nov 19. At the top of the range the offering raises about $64B and values Anthropic near $1.4T. The prospectus shows $33.2B in revenue for the first nine months of 2026.

items.headline: UK MPs call for an AI Safety and Security Bill with a regulator that can block risky models
items.summary: The Commons Business and Trade Committee's report, "Guardrails for Growth", proposes an enforcement body that could halt high-risk training and testing or block deployments. The AI Security Institute would keep doing the testing. These are recommendations only, and the government has not committed to them.

items.headline: Unconfirmed: Bank CEOs and NSA reportedly told Congress that rushed patches for AI-found bugs caused this week's outages
items.summary: The Washington Sun, citing three unnamed sources, reports that officials blamed outages at banks, airlines and NSA networks on the rush to fix floods of AI-discovered vulnerabilities, not on AI itself. The NSA publicly blamed routine maintenance, and the FAA administrator reportedly said there was "zero evidence" of an AI link.
